deep.reconstruction:
Context: Göttingen, evening of 1 May 1820. The year is inferred from the 1819 mean places used and the April–May ephemeris tables on the previous page. The previous page ends with 'Nachmittag stark an das Fernrohr gestossen' (in the afternoon the telescope was knocked hard). This page opens 'Wegen des erwähnten Stosses neu nivellirt' (because of that knock, re-levelled). The page reduces Reichenbach meridian-circle observations: clock corrections from transits, and the latitude from zenith distances.

(1) Level / zero point. The new level readings of the three verniers are 3'22.1", 3'31.7" and 3'15.5". These serve as the zero (index) readings Z1, Z2, Z3. 'Result 3'22"2' and 'a = i - 4"2' are level/collimation bookkeeping whose exact rule I cannot reconstruct. The plain mean of the three readings is 3'23.1".

(2) Clock corrections, Δt = (observed transit time) - (apparent RA).
- Capella: 5h3m13.67s - 5h3m14.16s = -0.49s.
- Sirius: three-wire times 36m49.2s, 37m6.1s, 37m22.9s. Their mean (my step) is 6h37m6.07s. The apparent RA is written as 6.795 + 0.076 (reduction from mean to apparent place). Gauss writes 6h37m6.77s and gets Δt = 6.07 - 6.77 = -0.70s.
- Castor: wires (38.1, 57.2, 76.9) give a mean of 57.40s. Apparent RA = 57.262 + 0.620 = 57.882s, so Δt = -0.48s.
- Procyon: wires (29.1, 45.1, 61.3) give 45.17s. Apparent RA = 45.292 + 0.523 = 45.815s, so Δt = -0.65s.
- Pollux: wires (50.5, 68.9, 87.8) give 9.07s. Apparent RA = 8.941 + 0.657 = 9.598s, so Δt = -0.53s.

(3) Refraction factors.
- Barometer 27 Par. inches 7.5 lines = 331.5 lines. log(331.5/336) + 10 = 9.99415 (my identification: 336 lines = 28 Par. inches as the standard pressure).
- Temperature factor: log 9.99090 at +14.5°R (Sirius) and 9.99310 at +13.4°R (the other stars). These are consistent with a standard temperature near 10°R.
- Combined factors: 9.98505 for Sirius and 9.98725 for the others.
- Logs of mean refraction: Sirius 2.15293 (about 142.2" at z ≈ 68°); Castor 1.30535; Procyon 1.77517; Pollux 1.39235.
- True refractions (my step for Sirius): Sirius 10^(2.15293 - 0.01495) ≈ 137.3". Compare the 137.40" entered for 1 May on the previous page.
- Castor 10^(1.30535 - 0.01275) = 19.62"; Procyon 57.87"; Pollux 23.97". These are written in the second column.

(4) Zenith distances.
- Verniers 2 and 3 record only the minutes modulo 5' plus seconds. For example, Castor 3'40.1" means 18'40.1" (my interpretation).
- Castor: z = mean over the three verniers of (reading - zero) = mean(15'5.0", 15'8.4", 15'3.2"). Added to 19°, this gives 19°15'5.53" (written 5.54).
- Procyon: mean(50'13.8", 50'17.3", 50'12.0") = 45°50'14.37" (written 14.45).
- Pollux: mean(4'12.1", 4'14.6", 4'11.9") = 23°4'12.87" (written 12.89).
- Sirius (my step): mean(-98.2", -94.3", -101.2") relative to 68° gives 67°58'22.1". The previous page's table has 67°58'22.27" for 1 May.
- Adding refraction: Castor 19°15'25.16", Procyon 45°51'12.32", Pollux 23°4'36.86".
- Adding the reduction to the 1819 mean place: Castor +17.7", Procyon +10.59", Pollux +17.64". The Pollux value matches the previous page's table for ~1 May.
- Results: Procyon 45°51'22.91", Pollux 23°4'54.50". Castor's value, 19°15'42.86", is implied but not written.

(5) Latitude for south-culminating stars, φ = z + δ(1819).
- Procyon: 45°51'22.91" + 5°40'53.84" = 51°32'16.75".
- Pollux: 23°4'54.50" + 28°27'15.55" ('Pond' = Pond's catalogue) = 51°32'10.05".
- Castor: 19°15'42.86" + 32°16'29.6" = 51°32'12.46", written 12.5.
- For comparison, the previous page gives Sirius on 1 May as 51°32'13.20".

This is routine meridian-circle reduction: clock error, refraction with barometer and thermometer factors, vernier means, and latitude from zenith distances of known-declination stars.
errors: Sirius apparent RA: as transcribed, 6.795 + 0.076 = 6.871, but Gauss writes 6.77 and Δt = -0.70. Either the first figure is really 6.695 (a misreading), or this is an addition slip; in the latter case Δt would be -0.80s.

Procyon zenith distance: the vernier differences average to 50'14.37", but 14.45" is written over a correction. Pollux is similar (12.87 vs 12.89). These small 0.02–0.08" differences may come from an unrecorded level correction.

The 'Result 3'22"2' for the zero point does not equal the plain mean of the three level readings (3'23.1"). The rule used is unclear; the zenith distances, however, agree with differencing each vernier against its own zero.

The latitude values (≈51°32'10"–17") lie ~25" above the accepted latitude of the Göttingen observatory (51°31'48"). This indicates an instrumental or zero-point systematic in these early meridian-circle results, not an arithmetic slip on this page.

results.what: Clock correction from transits of fundamental stars (mean of three wires minus apparent RA)

results.what: Refraction = mean refraction × barometric factor (b/336 lines) × thermometric factor, done in logarithms
results.modern_name: Atmospheric refraction correction with pressure/temperature factors

results.what: Latitude φ = z + δ from zenith distances of Castor, Procyon, Pollux and Sirius, reduced to 1819 mean places

deep.surprise_reason: Purely routine observatory reduction (clock error, refraction, vernier means, latitude) from Gauss's known work with the Reichenbach meridian circle at Göttingen around 1820; nothing mathematically novel.

checkable.asserts: barometric log factor ≈ 9.99415 for 27 in 7.5 lines vs 28 in
Castor mean vernier excess over 15' = 5.53" (verniers minus zero: 5.0, 8.4, 3.2)

transcription_corrections: 'Wagen' should read 'Wegen' (Wegen des erwähnten Stosses neu nivellirt).
'27^z 7'5' means barometer 27 Zoll 7.5 Linien; '+14"5' / '+13"4' are thermometer readings in °Réaumur, not arcseconds.
The second and third vernier readings (e.g. Castor 3'40.1, Pollux 2'46.3) are minutes modulo 5' plus seconds, not errors. The Pollux '2,46.3' and '2,27.4' are therefore correct as written.
Sirius apparent RA '6.37.6,795' may actually be '6.37.6,695', which is consistent with the written 6.77 and -0.70.
Procyon zenith distance '45.50.14.45' and Castor '19°15'5"54' are written over earlier figures.
